races.name: William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Cristo
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 23-day break under Pat Dobbs, faces prominent congestion but suits tactical finish
runners_data.comment: Handicapping case can be made but latest effort didn't suggest he's about to capitalise
runners_data.spotlight: Went back-to-back over 1m2f on Chelmsford's AW around this time last year; winless since and latest eighth of ten at Ripon (1m2f, good to soft) didn't suggest he's about to capitalise on a declining mark; a handicapping case can be made, though.

runners_data.name: Sweet Reward
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent Newbury second, veteran knows the game under 5lb claimer
runners_data.comment: Might not improve for comeback second (8.5f) but this trip is more suitable; each-way shot
runners_data.spotlight: Registered his seventh win when scoring on reappearance at Newbury (1m2f, good) last year and he attracted support before finishing second to an unexposed sort at Epsom (8.5f, good) on recent comeback this time; might not come on a bundle for that but this trip is more suitable and he's in with an each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Towerlands
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from 36-day break, recent AW form suggests Tony Carroll has him ready
runners_data.comment: Hat-trick once back on AW; chance depends on what he makes of this return to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Improved once returned to AW and bagged a hat-trick across October and December (1m); on the scoresheet again upped to 9.5f at Wolverhampton (career-best form) in February; form took a slight dip on last two starts, while his earlier turf form isn't comparable so interesting to see how he fares back on grass.

runners_data.name: Twisting Physics
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced prominent runner who raced keenly at Newbury, step up in trip may calm him
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced, progressive 5yo who made eye-catching return three weeks ago; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced, progressive 5yo; made all for narrow win at Newbury (7f) last June and shaped encouragingly upped to 1m2f back there (also good), racing freely but keeping on well from a poor draw on reappearance three weeks ago; retains plenty of potential.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in career-best form with recent Goodwood win, perfectly positioned tactically

runners_data.name: Noble Horizon
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning after 210-day break, makes all if retaining fitness edge
runners_data.comment: Bought for 140,000gns after good 3rd of 19 (10.5f, good; not clear run) in October; player
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent for William Haggas and he made all to land Leicester novice (1m2f, good to firm) in July; signed off for that yard with creditable third of 19 at York (10.5f, good; not clear run) off this mark in October; secured for 140,000gns a fortnight later and subsequently gelded; a player on stable debut/reappearance.

runners_data.name: Morcar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finished third in this race last year, solid course form but inconsistent lately
runners_data.comment: Good C&D record; won this last year; looks sure to be primed for this race again
runners_data.spotlight: Close third in this in 2024 and he enhanced a good C&D record when winning last year's edition (good to firm) from this mark; placed on his next four starts and had a soft-ground excuse on final start that term; had wind surgery ahead of a quiet comeback at Newbury three weeks ago but no surprise if this day has been ringed in his calendar.

runners_data.name: Youthful King
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form was 2022/23, question marks over current ability after poor finale
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on final start last term and two runs (1m4f) this season weren't encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time winner at 1m2f (good to firm) although that was back in 2022/23 and his last success came over 1m6f at Sandown in July; tailed off on final start last term and two runs (1m4f) this season contained little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Double Red
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong 2024 record including course win, Henry Candy team in poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Fourth win when scoring on return; up 5lb and this is tougher but he's progressive
runners_data.spotlight: Hit the ground running last year, winning twice at Nottingham in April, over 8.5f (good) and 1m2f (good to firm); also scored at Epsom (good to soft) in September and once again made a winning return when picking up an AW handicap here (1m2f) 19 days ago; up 5lb and this is tougher but he's progressive and can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Warning Sign
runners_data.note: Prominent racer better in amateur events, 7lb claimer booking suggests connections lack confidence
runners_data.comment: Won two amateur riders' races last year; of more interest when returned to that sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Won two amateur riders' races last year but not competitive in either start this term; suspicion he'll come back to life returned to those earlier events when owner David Dunsdon is back in the saddle.

races.paceDynamic: Noble Horizon will dictate terms from the front with no obvious early challengers for the lead. Sweet Reward, Twisting Physics, Morcar and Warning Sign will jostle for prominent positions behind the leader, creating a congested pack tracking the pace. The moderate early tempo should quicken from 3f out as the prominent group closes on Noble Horizon. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the mid-race congestion and deliver late challenges once the prominent runners have committed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack applies sustained pressure from 3f out creating a messy finish
scenarios.body: The early pace will be honest but not fierce, allowing closers to get into contention while the prominent runners get tangled up in traffic. Hold-up specialists can weave through beaten horses and time their challenges perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Position Perfect
scenarios.trigger: If Sweet Reward or Twisting Physics secure the ideal tracking position behind Noble Horizon
scenarios.body: One of the prominent runners avoids the congestion and has first run on the leader turning for home. The winner comes from this tactical position with enough left to repel late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Noble Horizon Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the leader maintains a decisive advantage turning into the straight
scenarios.body: Noble Horizon's uncontested lead proves insurmountable as the field leaves their challenges too late on the testing ground. The front-runner has enough in reserve to hold off all challengers despite the extended trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Noble Horizon sets pedestrian fractions and the field comes home in a bunch
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish with little separation between runners entering the final furlong. Any horse with a turn of foot can prevail regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: Noble Horizon's market support given the 210-day absence will reveal stable confidence in his fitness
Sweet Reward and Twisting Physics both want prominent positions and could compromise each other's chances
Cristo's headgear change to a pacifier suggests connections want him to settle better in hold-up role
Morcar needs to bounce back from his latest poor effort to repeat last year's course success
The 5lb and 7lb claiming jockeys on Sweet Reward and Warning Sign indicate connections managing expectations

races.name: William Hill Oaks Trial Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Romantic Symphony
runners_data.note: Sister to top-class performers with perfect recent form, but needs to prove stamina beyond 1m2f in her third career start.
runners_data.comment: 2-2 in novice events at Newmarket (1m, good) and Kempton (1m3f, AW); lots of potential
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to winners including Yibir (7f-2m including US Grade 1; RPR 123) and Wild Illusion (1m/1m2f including Group 1, also Oaks second; 116); 10-11 when getting the better of a pretty useful rival at Newmarket (1m, good) last September, preceding another novice win at much shorter odds in good style for six-runner race at Kempton (1m3f, AW) one month ago; lots of potential.

runners_data.name: Bloom
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with strong stamina breeding should relish uncontested lead, though 71-3 form line shows some inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Front-running third of seven in Group 3 at Navan (1m2f, good to yielding) two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: By Wootton Bassett out of a 9.5f Listed winner who's sister to Irish Guineas winner Roderic O'Connor; won a maiden at Cork (1m, yielding) last September and probably improved again when front-running third of seven in Group 3 at Navan (1m2f, good to yielding) two weeks ago; top trainer so often gets these 3yo middle-distance fillies to improve.

runners_data.name: Amora Queen
runners_data.note: Solid prominent runner with proven class but question marks over distance effectiveness after Group 1 failure.
runners_data.comment: Last in Group 1 Fillies' Mile; 2nd in 1m2f handicap at Doncaster is the best RPR in this
runners_data.spotlight: Won last summer on her first two starts, before failing to beat a rival in the Group 1 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket (33-1); second of six when favourite for a handicap at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) two weeks ago put her back on the right track and she's likely to stay; it's also the best RPR in this line-up but it would still be surprising if she's not vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Prizeland
runners_data.note: Only hold-up horse with Derby-winning family stamina, but needs significant pace collapse to be effective from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Won AW novice events over 1m and 1m4f; radically different opposition but she's promising
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to 2022 Derby second Hoo Ya Mal; made an eye-catching debut (good to soft) before her novice win at Kempton (1m, AW) later in October; 4-7 for another novice here (1m4f, AW) last month and easily dismissed her only three rivals in slowly run race; faces radically different opposition today and returns to turf but she's promising, for sure.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien second string with tactical speed but poor recent form suggests she may struggle at this level.
runners_data.comment: Reappearance fifth in 1m Curragh Group 3 was her best form; looks a middle-distance filly
runners_data.spotlight: Wootton Bassett half-sister to a 1m4f Listed winner; won 7f maiden at the Curragh before below-form favourite in a 1m Group 3 later in October; fifth of ten in another 1m Group 3 there on reappearance was her best form and suggested she's a middle-distance filly; those last three runs were in the mud, which is most unlikely here, but another step forward otherwise looks assured; Ryan Moore rides her for the first time.

races.paceDynamic: Bloom is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should set an uncontested lead at a sustainable tempo over this stamina test. Romantic Symphony, Amora Queen, and Cameo are all prominent racers who will track behind without applying early pressure, while Prizeland is the sole hold-up horse starting from the rear. The lack of genuine pace pressure should create a tactical affair where the tempo builds gradually into a finish that tests stamina credentials. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can position close enough to strike but avoid any late kick from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Bloom gets an easy lead and maintains a steady gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to conserve energy and resist late challenges over this stamina-sapping distance. Bloom's superior TopSpeed rating of 94 becomes decisive in a finish where positioning trumps pure acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Symphony and Amora Queen both track the leader perfectly and outstay her
scenarios.body: The Godolphin and Johnston fillies can use their higher RPR ratings (109/110) to wear down Bloom in the final furlong. Their prominent style perfectly suits a race where early positioning is crucial but late stamina tells.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Prizeland can use her Derby-winning family stamina to power through a slowly-run race that becomes tactical. Her fresh condition (25 days off) and hold-up style could be lethal if the tempo becomes stop-start.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: O'Brien Duo Control
scenarios.trigger: If both Bloom and Cameo work in tandem to control the race
scenarios.body: The master trainer's two runners can dictate terms with Bloom leading and Cameo tracking, before the latter strikes late. This tactical deployment maximizes their chances by eliminating pace worries entirely.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Bloom gets a soft lead through the first half-mile - she could prove unstoppable with uncontested fractions
Monitor Romantic Symphony's position turning for home - if she's within two lengths she has the class to win
Check Prizeland's early position - if she's closer than usual it suggests connections expect a truly-run race
Observe the pace through the middle section - any slowdown dramatically improves the hold-up horse's chances
Watch for Ryan Moore's tactics on Cameo - any aggressive move suggests she's better than recent form indicates

races.name: William Hill Lingfield Derby Trial Stakes (Listed Race) (Colts & Geldings)

runners_data.name: Maltese Cross
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected strong pace, Marquand excels with this tactical approach, 22 days since impressive Newmarket win ideal
runners_data.comment: Good chance he will come on from recent Newbury win and be suited by this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Went close on debut at Ascot (1m, soft) and beat notable rivals in a Newmarket maiden (1m, good) later in September; favourite for a valuable novice event at Newbury (1m2f, good) three weeks ago and battled his way to another narrow win, in a blanket finish but there's a good chance he will come on from that run and be suited by this longer trip (very much supported by pedigree); firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Classic O'Brien hold-up runner with Moore aboard, Group 1 fourth when staying on late suggests this trip and pace scenario ideal
runners_data.comment: Fourth in French Group 1 (1m2f, very soft) in October; shaped as if needing race on return
runners_data.spotlight: Camelot colt; maiden winner at Glorious Goodwood and best form when staying on from off the pace to take fourth in Group 1 Criterium de Saint-Cloud (1m2f, very soft) in October; shaped as if he needed the race when fourth of seven from the back in Listed event at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on return, and this is a different trip, so it's far too early to write him off.

runners_data.name: Maho Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with two authoritative wins, Buick will need to judge fractions carefully against other pace angles
runners_data.comment: He's made a striking 2-2 start to his career with wins in a 1m3f maiden and 1m2f novice
runners_data.spotlight: Hot favourite when winning with great authority in five-runner races for a maiden at Kempton (1m3f, AW; led 2f out) in December and novice event at Newmarket (1m2f, good; made all) in April, beating O'Brien and Gosden runners in the latter; Dubawi colt with speed on the dam's side but he's won over 1m3f already and has made a striking start to his career.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Brilliance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 194-day break, two wins came when handy rather than held up, fitness question after long absence
runners_data.comment: 1m2f/1m1f winner as 2yo, latterly making all and stretching 8l clear in a Redcar novice
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to smart Flat and hurdle winner Absurde; odds-on winner of maiden at Goodwood (1m2f, soft) and novice at Redcar (1m1f, good to soft) on last two starts as 2yo, in the latter making all and stretching 8l clear; needs a good deal better in this company but he's clearly promising.

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Natural leader who won when making all at Lingfield recently, 11 days since last run keeps him sharp for another front-running effort
runners_data.comment: Rallying third of six in 1m2f Listed race at Epsom suggested this longer trip would suit
runners_data.spotlight: Winning siblings include Claymore, a Group 3 winner at 1m2f for this yard; third to Maltese Cross in a 1m Newmarket maiden on sole 2yo start; evens when making all in a Kempton novice (1m, AW) on return and his rallying third of six in Listed race at Epsom (1m2f, good) suggested that this longer trip would suit; some others have better form but he can improve.

runners_data.name: A Taste Of Glory
runners_data.note: Front runner stepping up significantly in class, lowest official rating but recent confidence-boosting win at this track helps
runners_data.comment: 1m2f win here (AW) came by a neck off a mark of just 80 but the second has won twice since
runners_data.spotlight: It was a French Group 1 (1m2f, very soft) which saw his progress arrested as a 2yo; his improved form to win a six-runner handicap here (1m2f, AW) on reappearance came by a neck off a mark of just 80 and although the runner-up has won twice since, this race clearly demands big improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Maho Bay, Balzac, and A Taste Of Glory will ensure a strong early gallop in this small but competitive field, with all three having confirmed front-running tendencies. The pace will be honest throughout the 1m3½f trip, particularly with Maho Bay's authority from the front and Balzac's recent tactical speed. Isaac Newton and Maltese Cross will be held up off this pace by Moore and Marquand respectively, while Bay Of Brilliance sits prominent but not engaged early. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce sustained finishes, as the pace pressure will stretch the field and create opportunities for closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front runners (Maho Bay, Balzac, A Taste Of Glory) engage early and maintain strong fractions
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses to deliver telling late runs. Isaac Newton and Maltese Cross, with their proven ability to finish strongly, will benefit most from this likely unfolding.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Maho Bay or Balzac can dictate fractions and kick clear in the straight
scenarios.body: One of the classier front runners uses tactical speed to control the race and has enough left to resist late challenges. Maho Bay's recent authority or Balzac's versatility could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Success
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Of Brilliance can sit handy and avoid the early pace battle
scenarios.body: The Ralph Beckett runner gets the perfect trip tracking the leaders without engaging early, then outstays them in the final furlong. His two wins came when prominent, making this scenario plausible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Misjudged Completely
scenarios.trigger: If all three front runners go too slow early or A Taste Of Glory surprises with improved form
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the lowest-rated runner's recent win gives him confidence. This would require significant pace misjudgment from the market leaders.

watchPoints.text: Maho Bay and Balzac engaging in early speed battle could compromise both front runners' finishing kicks
Bay Of Brilliance showing any signs of needed conditioning run after 194-day layoff in preliminary movements
Isaac Newton's position turning for home - Moore needs to avoid being caught too far back if pace collapses quickly
A Taste Of Glory attempting to match the class leaders for early speed despite significant ratings gap
Track bias favoring any particular part of the course given good to firm conditions across all races today

races.name: William Hill Chartwell Fillies' Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: La Brodeuse
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario but 181 days off the track creates fitness concerns for Tom Marquand.
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; unraced at 7f and on good or quicker; unexposed; market revealing on yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French filly who didn't run as 2yo; won at Chantilly (1m, soft) on her debut last May; creditable effort despite not staying 1m2f at Listed level next time and she left Andre Fabre for 125,000euros after midfield finish in Saint-Cloud Listed race (1m, heavy) in November; unraced on good or quicker ground but not fully exposed and interesting to see how she goes in the market on this stable debut and first start at 7f.

runners_data.name: Mandurah
runners_data.comment: Good to firm suits; useful C&D form in Group 3 as a 2yo; new yard; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Winning 2yo debut was followed by a stout effort in a Group 3 over C&D (also good to firm) when leading from some way out and looked like holding on but couldn't quite sustain her effort; has rarely had her ground since but she ran well against an improver on AW (7f) in October on final start for the Crisfords; sold for 150,000gns; she might well have a good 4yo season.

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to track Copacabana Sands but tough 6-year-old mare faces younger, less exposed rivals.
runners_data.comment: Fifth win when landing h'cap (7f, good) last time; bit to do but can make presence felt
runners_data.spotlight: Tough mare who won two handicaps around this time last year, scoring at Windsor (6f, good to firm) and following up at Goodwood (7f, good) 18 days later; registered plenty of other good efforts last term and was back on the scoresheet with narrow win at Yarmouth (7f, good) 11 days ago; something to find on the figures but she's the type to make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Fouette
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer benefits from pace shape though returns from 36-day break which may blunt her finishing kick slightly.
runners_data.comment: Career best when fifth in Deauville Listed (7.5f, AW) in December; still has work to do
runners_data.spotlight: All three starts at 7f on good to firm and good as 2yo, winning Yarmouth maiden in July; reappeared from 425-day break to land two 7f AW handicaps in October and career-best form when fifth of 16 in Deauville Listed event (7.5f, AW) in December; beat only one home in a valuable handicap at Newcastle on last month's return, however, and has work to do in this company.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Classic closer with strong form on good/good to firm going but 202-day absence raises fitness questions for Ralph Beckett.
runners_data.comment: Big run when unlucky second in Ascot Listed (7f, soft) in October; respected on return
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning handicap debut at Kempton (AW) on her return last May and scored again at Thirsk (good) in September; fine effort despite not getting the breaks when just denied in Ascot Listed event (also 7f, soft) the following month and midfield finish from a poor draw at Longchamp a fortnight later is easily glossed over; commands respect on this return.

runners_data.name: Copacabana Sands
runners_data.note: Front-running style means she controls the race but Ryan Moore must judge fractions perfectly to repel late challengers.
runners_data.comment: Won Leopardstown Group 3 in June; sets the standard on first start for Andrew Balding
runners_data.spotlight: Seems tactically versatile; hooded when winning Naas Listed event (good) last May and followed up in Leopardstown Group 3 (also 7f, soft) the following month; left Michael O'Callaghan (same owner) after disappointing on heavy ground in October; Ryan Moore booked and she sets the standard on this stable debut/reappearance; plenty to like.

runners_data.name: Royal Velvet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in ideal tactical position with recent Newmarket win providing confidence for William Buick partnership.
runners_data.comment: 8-time winner who aims to progress out of handicaps; ceiling of ability yet to be reached
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive mare who scored for the eighth time when beating 18-runner field at Newmarket (7f, good) at last month's Craven meeting; might need some luck in running if the field gravitates to the stands' side but thoroughly deserves this first crack at a Pattern race, with the ceiling of her ability probably yet to be reached.

runners_data.name: Sunlit Uplands
runners_data.note: Another hold-up performer but 170-day break and moderate recent form make her vulnerable to sharper rivals.
runners_data.comment: Progressive; signed off for Rae Guest with fourth in 1m AW Listed here (1m); watch market
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive novice (6f, AW) and dual handicap winner (7f, good and soft) who signed off for Rae Guest with solid fourth of ten in Listed event on AW here (1m) in November; can likely do better again with just eight starts behind her; stable debut.

races.paceDynamic: Copacabana Sands will take them along from the front with Mandurah (non-runner) out, leaving Havana Pusey as the main pace companion in a small field. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching with only one confirmed front-runner and limited early pressure. This tactical scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver late kicks, as the pace-setters will have plenty left in the tank turning for home. The race shape clearly benefits closers and hold-up performers over early pace horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalize Late
scenarios.trigger: If Copacabana Sands sets uncontested fractions and the pace proves too slow for front-runners to sustain their advantage
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade get ideal conditions to unleash finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. Royal Velvet, Dash Of Azure and La Brodeuse can exploit the tactical advantage of racing off a steady pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Copacabana Sands uses her Group-level class to control the race and kick clear when challenged
scenarios.body: With limited early pressure, she dictates terms throughout and has enough left to repel late challengers. Her Listed and Group 3 victories at this trip in Ireland prove her effectiveness when allowed to dominate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Pusey tracks Copacabana Sands and times her challenge perfectly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The 6-year-old mare uses her experience to sit second throughout before striking late. Her recent Goodwood win shows she can capitalize when getting the right racing position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so slow that it becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of position
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where tactical positioning matters less than raw finishing speed. Horses with natural pace like Sunlit Uplands can benefit from the chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Copacabana Sands setting fractions that are too slow early, allowing the closers to swamp her in the final furlong
Royal Velvet getting trapped behind horses in the straight after her recent Newmarket success showed she needs racing room
La Brodeuse and Dash Of Azure showing any signs of ring-rustiness after their lengthy absences from the track
The pace becoming genuinely slow early, turning this into a sprint finish where draw and luck-in-running become crucial
Havana Pusey's positioning behind Copacabana Sands, as she needs to track the leader closely to time her challenge

races.name: William Hill Each Way Extra Handicap

runners_data.name: Back In Black
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from 21-day break with strong recent form but needs the pace to develop to be effective
runners_data.comment: Career best when fourth on his return three weeks ago; doesn't know how to run a bad race
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on his reappearance at Newbury (7f) last April; string of good efforts followed from August onwards and he posted a career best when fourth of 24 in Newbury's Spring Cup (1m, also good) on his return three weeks ago; stall 1 might not be ideal but otherwise holds strong claims.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning after 224-day absence but has winning form at this distance and strong course record
runners_data.comment: Dual AW winner last year; career-high mark but acts on turf and respected on this return
runners_data.spotlight: Good second of 16 (AW) on his stable debut/reappearance last April and went on to land similar events in June and July; turf no issue and was second of 17 at Ascot (also 1m, soft; acts on good to firm) in September; career-high mark but still respected on this return.

runners_data.name: Apotheosis
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good turf form who can press the pace and has recent winning momentum from Newcastle
runners_data.comment: 7f 3yo winner here; beaten neck at Abu Dhabi latest; career-high mark but still considered
runners_data.spotlight: Defied penalty in 3yo novice here (good) in 2024; back from a 145-day break and wind surgery when landing Class 2 at Newcastle (also 7f, AW) in December and beaten a neck at Abu Dhabi (1m, good) in March; career-high mark but still considered.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing retained blinkers with solid AW form here but needs to settle and find his kick
runners_data.comment: Respectable ninth in Lincoln and third at Newmarket's Craven meeting; can't be ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Novice and handicap (7f) winner on AW here, latterly in December when sporting first-time blinkers (retained); respectable ninth of 21 when 66-1 for the Lincoln in March and it was another solid effort when third in Class 2 handicap (1m, good) at Newmarket's Craven meeting; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: The Dragon King
runners_data.note: Patient type with decent recent form who needs strong pace to unleash his finishing effort effectively
runners_data.comment: Narrow defeat (7f, AW) in February was up with his best form; not dismissed back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Spectacular late run to land valuable auction race (6f, good to soft) in October 2024 is starting to fade from the memory but he won his first race since when taking a Wolverhampton handicap in November; narrow defeat at Newcastle (also 7f, AW) in February was up with his best form and respectable efforts on last two starts; not dismissed back on turf.

runners_data.name: Dragon Leader
runners_data.note: Forward-going sort who has been finding his level recently and can track the early pace
runners_data.comment: No win since 2023 but ran well latest and drawn to bag the near rail; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in very valuable auction race as a juvenile but winless since taking Redcar's Two-Year-Old Trophy six weeks later; looked to be rediscovering his level when third on AW in March and it was a solid fifth of 18 behind Royal Velvet (declared for preceding Group 3) at Newmarket (7f, good) last time; if the stands' rail proves the place to be this could be the day to revert to forcing tactics; interesting.

runners_data.name: Sword
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 204-day break wearing hood, needs everything to fall right from poor draw
runners_data.comment: Capable in a hood when on a going day last term; makes yard debut in tongue-tie this time
runners_data.spotlight: Patchy form for David O'Meara last term but won in June (good to firm; first-time hood) and ran a corker when third of 21 in valuable Ascot handicap (good) in July; back in form when slightly unlucky second at Newcastle (also 7f, AW) in October and sold for 40,000gns later that month; hood (absent when disappointing on final start) missing again; tongue tied for stable debut and warrants a market check.

runners_data.name: Foreseen
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with recent good form who acts on the surface but needs genuine pace development
runners_data.comment: The winner of three of his last six starts; this is hotter than his normal patch, though
runners_data.spotlight: The winner of three of his last six starts (1m, heavy and AW) and ran another solid race when close fourth of ten here (AW) in March; also acts on good ground but this is hotter than the races he usually contests.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Swivell will likely lead from the start with his prominent style, potentially joined early by Apotheosis and Dragon Leader who both show forward tendencies. With only one confirmed front-runner, Mr Swivell can dictate a comfortable pace without early pressure, allowing the large contingent of hold-up horses (Back In Black, Christian David, The Dragon King, Sword, Foreseen) to settle behind. The sustainable early gallop will create a tactical race where positioning becomes crucial in the straight. This pace setup strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace, as the hold-up brigade may find themselves with too much to do if the tempo doesn't truly develop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Swivell dictates an even tempo without serious early challenges
scenarios.body: The prominent runners maintain their positional advantage while the hold-up horses struggle to close the gap in time. Tactical pace and positioning trump raw finishing speed over this 7½f trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely testing and spreads the field
scenarios.body: The hold-up specialists find their finishing kicks more potent as the early pace-setters begin to tie up in the final furlong. Class and closing speed become the decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Pressure Changes
scenarios.trigger: If Apotheosis or Dragon Leader challenge Mr Swivell before halfway
scenarios.body: The increased tempo from 4f out creates the perfect setup for horses with tactical speed who can position just off the pace. Neither pure front-runners nor hold-up horses benefit optimally.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Scramble Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses engage in early speed duels
scenarios.body: The unsustainable early fractions completely change the complexion, allowing a patient outsider to pick up the pieces. Form and ratings become less relevant than race positioning.

watchPoints.text: Mr Swivell showing any signs of ring-rustiness after 224 days off as he's crucial to the pace development
Christian David's ability to settle properly in blinkers as he can get keen and compromise his finishing kick
The early battle between Apotheosis and Dragon Leader to track Mr Swivell as it could set up the race shape
Back In Black's positioning from his draw as he needs to be handy enough to strike when the pace develops
Sword's jumping and early alertness returning from such a long break in first-time hood for new connections

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap

runners_data.name: Oracle Mission
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 152 days off but showed good speed when winning here in December
runners_data.comment: Both starts here (7f, AW); good start and won next time; blinkers on for turf/h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Good start when third on AW here (7f) in November and didn't need to improve to beat 11 others returned to that C&D the following month; interesting to see blinkers go on for this handicap/turf debut but still of clear interest on his reappearance.

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: Free-running prominent type who pulled hard at Doncaster, needs restraint from Muscutt early doors
runners_data.comment: Has some potential but needs to settle better if he is to fulfill it
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in his qualifying runs; pulled hard when disappointing on handicap debut at Doncaster (good to soft) in September and raced freely when fourth in Wolverhampton novice (also 7f, AW) on his reappearance three weeks ago; now makes second handicap start and needs to settle if he's going to fulfill his potential.

runners_data.name: Dagger Strike
runners_data.note: Made all last time but equally effective tracking pace, fitted with cheekpieces for first time
runners_data.comment: Made all on handicap debut; form dipped latest but drawn to attack; second turf start
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded and well backed when making all on handicap debut at Newcastle in December; runner-up on his next three starts but form dipped at Southwell (also 7f, AW) towards the end of March; having just his second go on turf and could be well drawn to attack.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace, disappointing on handicap debut in testing conditions
runners_data.comment: Underwhelming h'cap debut on good to soft but much better when 2nd on return; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden and novice winner (6f, good to firm/good) last summer who was a shade disappointing when fifth of ten on handicap debut at Newbury (good to soft) in September; subsequently gelded and his neck second of 13 at Newmarket (also 7f, good) was much more like it on his comeback last month; mixed messages have come out of that race but still commands plenty of respect.

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: Can lead but lacks early pace over further than 6f, returning after 148 days absence
runners_data.comment: Can lead; Naas maiden (6f, good) winner in August; could be well drawn on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Can lead; Naas maiden (6f, good) winner in August for Michael O'Callaghan who wasn't disgraced in a brief two-race spell on AW for Ken Condon; bought for 18,000gns in January; potentially in the best stall and sole start at 7f was inconclusive so heed the market signals on this stable debut/reappearance.

runners_data.name: Mystic Moment
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who benefits from strong gallop, struggling since stable transfer to Mulholland
runners_data.comment: Useful for previous yard; will need to put stable debut behind her in this first handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Useful filly for Eve Johnson Houghton, readily made all in Epsom maiden (7f, good; Assaranca 4l second) in July; transferred to Neil Mulholland (same owners) but it was a low-key start when last of six in conditions race at Kempton (1m, AW) on her comeback in March; needs to put that behind her on this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: French Affair
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who handles this track well, bounced back to form at Kempton in March
runners_data.comment: Backward step last time was a little out of character so probably worth forgiving
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on handicap debut at Newbury (6f, good) in August and it was a good return when just failing at Kempton in March; took a big step backwards at Southwell (also 7f, AW) next time, although that was a little out of character so probably worth forgiving.

runners_data.name: Assaranca
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner carrying just 125lbs, in good form since seasonal return at Epsom
runners_data.comment: Made all in October; fair effort latest; could be dangerous if she grabs the stands' rail
runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Nottingham in October under Joe Leavy and she stepped up on her seasonal return when third of six at Epsom (also 8.5f, good) 11 days ago; could be dangerous if she grabs the stands' rail.

races.paceDynamic: Assaranca will make the running from stall with only Fresh Fade showing any inclination to lead, though she lacks early pace at 5f-6f. Oracle Mission, Mr Writer, Dagger Strike and French Affair will settle prominent behind the pace-setter, creating a reasonable gallop but nothing fierce with only one committed front-runner. The small field and single leader means moderate fractions early before quickening from 2f out as the prominent runners close. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers who can track Assaranca and kick clear, rather than the hold-up horses who will struggle for a strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace allows prominent horses to travel strongly and kick clear from 2f out
scenarios.body: Oracle Mission, Dagger Strike and Mr Writer can track Assaranca perfectly before unleashing superior finishing kicks. Hardy's Hero and Mystic Moment will find insufficient pace to close the gap from their hold-up positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Assaranca maintains her advantage despite pressure from the prominent pack turning for home
scenarios.body: Her light weight and recent good form at Epsom allows her to hold off challengers who leave their run fractionally late. The hold-up horses still struggle with insufficient pace to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack goes too hard trying to reel in Assaranca and tire in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Hardy's Hero and Mystic Moment benefit from the stronger pace created by the early battle. Their class tells as they sweep past weakening leaders close home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Assaranca sets crawling fractions and no prominent horse wants to challenge until very late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the final 2f where pure speed matters most over tactical positioning. Fresh Fade's early pace becomes an asset in a slowly-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Assaranca breaks smartly and establishes clear lead before first bend as no other horse shows early speed
Mr Writer pulls hard early and forces Daniel Muscutt into restraining battle that compromises his finishing kick
Hardy's Hero gets further back than ideal if the early pace stays moderate around the bend
Dagger Strike's new cheekpieces cause him to race keener than usual in the early stages
Oracle Mission shows any signs of needing the run after his lengthy absence since December

races.name: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Maharajas Express
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, returning to turf after disappointing AW comeback run 12 days ago
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard and kept on well enough on return (6f, AW); much better expected back at 5f
runners_data.spotlight: The winner of three 5f handicaps for Ian Williams last season, the latest off just 1lb lower; never a threat on his seasonal return 12 days ago (6f, AW) but he kept on well enough given he took a fierce hold through the early part of the race; better expected back at 5f and with the reappearance run behind him.

runners_data.name: Shalaa Asker
runners_data.note: Hold-up style drawn wide with poor turf record, needs pace collapse but Tom Marquand booking is positive
runners_data.comment: Had a good winter on AW but he is just 1-28 on turf and stall 1 rarely a positive here
runners_data.spotlight: Nine wins on the AW but just 1-28 on turf; fit from a productive winter campaign but he's drawn on the outside and others are more appealing.

runners_data.name: My Boy Harry
runners_data.note: Hold-up type dropping back to 5f after 7f/8f winter campaign, needs everything to fall right from this trip
runners_data.comment: Two 7f AW wins in January; quiet more recently and the return to 5f is an obvious concern
runners_data.spotlight: In good form in the depths of winter, winning two 7f handicaps at Chelmsford; edging back down the weights after some below-par runs but returning to 5f, even in a race that is highly likely to be run at a fast pace, is unlikely to revive his fortutnes.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good form who can sit handy and finish, Adam Kirby taking over training duties adds intrigue
runners_data.comment: Two wins on AW for new yard but ran well on turf at Catterick; up in weights but improving
runners_data.spotlight: Bolted up on his stable debut at Southwell in March (6f); dropped to 5f for his last two starts, picked off late at Catterick (good ground) before a ready win on the AW track here nine days ago; another 7lb higher mark to contend with but unlikely he has reached his ceiling just yet.

runners_data.name: Birkenhead
runners_data.note: Veteran front-runner who showed dash at Catterick despite weakening, will contest early lead with trademark pace
runners_data.comment: Retains plenty of dash and should make a bold bid up the stands' rail; place contender
runners_data.spotlight: Into the veteran stage but he retains plenty of dash, setting a good pace at Catterick 17 days ago before weakening into third (Tuscan Point second but 8lb worse off today); likely to make a beeline for the stands' rail and more minor money could be on the cards.

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with course and distance win on record, 6lb lower than last year's Newbury success but recent form poor
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; 6lb lower than for last summer's Newbury win; recent efforts not his best
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner with a C&D win on his record; 6lb lower than when seeing off seven rivals at Newbury last summer (5f, good to firm) but not easily recommended on 2026 evidence and he will find easier races to dominate than this.

runners_data.name: Desert Champion
runners_data.note: Prominent type with fading finish tendency, much lower mark than previous campaigns but hard to trust
runners_data.comment: On a reduced mark but it is easy enough to have reservations for now
runners_data.spotlight: Had a BHA mark 26lb higher than today when starting out for this yard last summer but he's struggled to make much of an impact; did finish second at Newcastle in November (well backed) but that form hasn't worked out at all; recent Redcar reappearance is easy to excuse (went off hard and raced in a group of two, finishing sixth and seventh, on the far side); stable looks to hold stronger claims with Birkenhead.

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better on all-weather, winless on turf in 15 attempts despite Hollie Doyle booking
runners_data.comment: 0-15 on turf; not at best on AW this spring and others bring more convincing claims
runners_data.spotlight: Has form on good to firm but 0-15 on grass as opposed to 5-29 on AW; short of his best on AW of late and others bring more convincing claims.

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won this race last year from ideal draw, flies from stalls but recent form lacks spark
runners_data.comment: Overcame a poor draw to win this race last year; 1lb lower today; one to take seriously
runners_data.spotlight: Turned in an excellent effort when winning the corresponding race from stall 1 (14 ran) last May, flying out of the stalls and able to get to the stands' rail after one furlong; also won at Ffos Las in July and both victories were achieved off a higher mark than today's; not at best last time but his reappearance had been encouraging; should make a bold bid.

races.paceDynamic: Birkenhead and So Smart are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, with Faustus and Desert Champion likely to press from prominent positions. The pace will be honest but not suicidal over this short trip, with the leaders setting a decent gallop before the field compacts turning for home. The relatively small field means pace won't be extreme, but the good to firm ground will allow sustained speed throughout. This race shape favours prominent racers and strong finishers who can position handy and kick, rather than pure front-runners or horses needing to come from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Birkenhead and So Smart go quick early and maintain pressure
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will stretch the field and favour horses with tactical speed who can sit close and finish strongly. Tuscan Point and Maharajas Express can benefit from the strong pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets an easy lead and kicks clear
scenarios.body: So Smart showed last year he can dictate from the front at this track, and if Birkenhead doesn't engage early enough, the leader could steal a march. The good ground will help sustain the effort to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too strong and both leaders tie up
scenarios.body: A fierce early battle between Birkenhead and So Smart could set up the race for a closer with finishing kick. The hold-up horses will need the pace to be unsustainable to get into contention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest and prominent racers can time their move
scenarios.body: Faustus could benefit from a position just behind the leaders if the pace is manageable, allowing him to use his course and distance experience. Desert Champion might also benefit despite his finishing concerns.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Birkenhead and So Smart engage in early speed duel that could set up race for closers
Watch Desert Champion's finishing effort as he tends to fade late despite prominent early positioning
Watch Shalaa Asker for market support given poor turf record but strong jockey booking with Tom Marquand
Watch pace development as small field could lead to tactical affair rather than honest gallop
Watch Tuscan Point's settling pattern as he drops back to 5f having shown best form over this trip recently
